subject.title: docs: propose plugin-owned external verification approvals

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this exact plugin-owned verifier contract as the permanent approval-resolution seam, including host-derived ownership, AND-style denial precedence, session grants, version gating, and audit lifecycle events?
rationale: The choice creates a security-sensitive plugin API and determines which component may attest verification while core commits protected execution; document review cannot safely choose that authority boundary.

options.title: Accept the narrowed contract
options.body: Approve the RFC direction subject to implementation proof for ownership binding, denial races, replay and idempotency, version gating, session grants, and audit metadata.

options.title: Narrow to allow-once
options.body: Permit external verification only for one-time approvals until session-trust and grant semantics receive separate evidence and review.

options.title: Reject the core seam
options.body: Keep external ceremonies outside the canonical approval state machine and require AgentKit to use existing plugin surfaces.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrowed contract
recommendation.body: Approve the RFC direction subject to implementation proof for ownership binding, denial races, replay and idempotency, version gating, session grants, and audit metadata.
